name: Grand Hotel Excelsior Vittoria
positioning: Family-owned clifftop hotel on Piazza Tasso in the heart of Sorrento, run by the Fiorentino family since 1834, with views over the Bay of Naples and Mount Vesuvius
best_for: Travelers who want a central Sorrento base for boat days to Capri and the Amalfi Coast
Guests drawn to a historic, family-run hotel with classic rooms
Food lovers who want terrace dining over the Bay of Naples

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Sorrento, on Piazza Tasso, with views over the Bay of Naples and Mount Vesuvius.
The hotel has been family-owned since 1834.
Fifth-generation members of the Fiorentino family now run the hotel.
Rooms are classic in style, with antique furniture and a Sorrentine palette of blues and whites.
Many rooms and suites have views over the Bay of Naples, and some have private terraces or balconies.
Terrazza Bosquet serves refined Mediterranean cuisine with panoramic views over the Bay of Naples.
Terrazza Vittoria serves Campanian produce at lunch, with simple plates such as spaghetti in San Marzano tomato sauce or lentil soup.
Breakfast is served under frescoes at Ristorante Vittoria, with homemade cakes and marmalades.
The spa has private spa suites with jacuzzi and outdoor areas.
Spa facials and massages use products from the Swiss brand Valmont.
Conde Nast Traveler named the hotel to its Gold List 2026.

highlights.text: Boutique Spa La Serra is set in the private gardens, inside a restored 19th-century greenhouse.
According to legend, the Roman emperor Augustus once built his villa on the hotel's site.
The hotel spans three buildings: La Vittoria, opened by the Fiorentino family in 1834, La Rivale from 1882, and the Swiss-style La Favorita from the early 20th century.
A private lift gives access toward the port area, convenient for boat days to Capri and along the coast.
The hotel's suites include the Pavarotti Suite, the Caruso Suite and the Margaret Suite, named for famous guests.

considerations.text: The hotel sits on a cliff above the sea in the town centre; guests reach the port area and seafront by a private lift.
Rooms are classic, with antique furniture, rather than contemporary in style.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's luxury positioning.
